pr_title: Analytic sphere-box, sphere-cylinder, and capsule-cylinder collisions
pr_body:
This addresses part of #70615.  It replaces the SAT code for three collision types with analytic solvers.  This tends to be faster and more accurate.

*Physics squad edit:*
- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70405
- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57476
pr_comments:
My testing shows:
 - sphere/box collision detection appears to work fine.
 - sphere/cylinder collision detection appears to work fine.
 - capsule/cylinder collision detection appears to work fine.

I did notice an unrelated effect however - when I move_and_collide the objects I'm getting different Z positions which makes it look like the objects are bouncing slightly. The position distance is only 0.015625 and I think it's caused by the GodotSpace3D::test_body_motion iterative walking loop; however it may explain why the Godot 4 VR games feel like the players height is bouncing up and down slightly.

As requested by @fabriceci in the physics contributors chat; I've started work on an automated test suite for physics collisions. It currently only has the following configurations:
 - sphere/sphere
 - sphere/cylinder
 - sphere/box
 - sphere/capsule
 - capsule/capsule

Running against Godot 4 beta 10 shows 9 test failures including capsule/capsule, sphere/capsule, sphere/cylinder
Running against #70660 shows the capsule/capsule and sphere/capsule is fixed
Running against #70787 shows the sphere/cylinder is fixed

I'll add more tests including the capsule/cylinder shortly.

That's excellent!  I've had it in mind for a while to write an automated test that would do the following.

- Loop over every possible combination of two primitive types.
- For each one, place them at a series of random positions and orientations and check for collisions.
- Repeat the check, replacing either or both objects with a high resolution mesh.
- Make sure they agree up to the accuracy of the mesh.

I've been waiting for #67481 to get merged first, since right now collisions on large meshes are too slow for that test to be practical.

I looked into the bouncing motion you mentioned.  It looks to me like this line in `GodotCollisionSolver3D::solve_distance()` is the problem:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/57267709e665f1683e79bd5d3432be2be5db6c1d/servers/physics_3d/godot_collision_solver_3d.cpp#L587

Even though we've created analytic routines to identify collisions, it's still hardcoded to use GJK at a key point in the process.

By the looks of things we have two classes of collision algorithm:
 - solve_static detects when shapes are colliding, and returns the "contact points" on the shapes
 - solve_distance detects when shapes are not colliding, and returns the "closest points" on the shape

All the existing collision functions (_collision_sphere_sphere, _collision_sphere_box, _collision_capsule_capsule, etc.) are used by solve_static to detect the contact points and only return the points if the shapes are touching.

It seems like we're going to need a new class of functions (_distance_sphere_sphere, _distance_sphere_box, _distance_capsule_capsule, etc) to detect the closest points. These new functions would be VERY similar to the current analytic functions; but would provide their results on separation rather than collision, and wouldn't need to provide the points with a callback function.

I was just about to post asking for clarification about that.  It isn't clear to me whether we really need the distance version.  The only place `solve_distance()` ever gets called is inside `GodotSpace3D::test_body_motion()`, and that function appears to ignore all of the return values except the boolean for whether the objects overlap.

The way it gets called is rather confusing.  If you look at `solve_distance()`, you'll see that `r_point_A`, `r_point_B`, and `r_sep_axis` are strictly output arguments.  It stores values into them.  It doesn't care what initial values they have.  But `test_body_motion()` sets them anyway and seems to expect them to be used.  For example,

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/61c7b7fb13f7cef8737d0a047db1c2340d1ce661/servers/physics_3d/godot_space_3d.cpp#L870-L871

Setting `sep` doesn't actually do anything at all.  The value just gets overwritten in the next line without ever being used.  It also records the values returned for the two nearest points

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/61c7b7fb13f7cef8737d0a047db1c2340d1ce661/servers/physics_3d/godot_space_3d.cpp#L884-L885

but then they immediately get thrown out without ever being used.

It looks to me like `solve_distance()` is unnecessary.  All we really need is to check whether the two shapes overlap or not.

I was thinking if we had an actual solve_distance() function we could use it like a ray-marcher for casting motion rather than the binary search approach used at the moment. I'm not certain how much of an improvement we would get in terms of the average number of iterations. At least the binary search algorithm is bounded in terms of iteration-count and distance error.

An easy way to get some of the same benefit is to call `project_range()` on each object to find the shortest and longest motion distances at which they could possibly intersect.  In many cases that should provide much tighter initial bounds for the search.

One other thought about it: if we can get accurate collision normals in all cases, we can use them to compute the derivative of the collision depth with respect to the motion distance.  That can be used to get faster convergence.
Very nice approach, and good discussion in the comments here about what can be done next. I'm working on cylinder-cylinder, so we'll be able to use an axis created by the closest points there too.

Just to leave a note for anyone who comes here after upgrading to beta 12 (or 4.0 I guess) and has physics issues with spheres, **really make sure** that you don't have a collision shape scaled from itself or any parent nodes, as the previous solver would let you get away with it and this one will not.

It highlighted a bug in my code that I thought I had previously solved. Hopefully this helps someone in the future.

Also thank you @peastman and @Malcolmnixon for the focus on physics.
@cridenour We should probably add a note in the documentation for this, and make an editor warning if a collision shape is scaled from itself or its parents.

issue_context.title: [GodotPhysics] CharacterBody3D gets stuck on flat ends of static cylinders
issue_context.body:
___

***Bugsquad note:** This issue has been confirmed several times already. No need to confirm it further.*

___

### Godot version

4.0

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Moving a CharacterBody3D along the flat end of a cylinder does not behave the same as sliding along a flat wall. The CharacterBody3D can even become stuck in place and unable to move away form the cylinder once it reaches the edges of the cylinder's flat surface
![CylinderIssue](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38251868/151744077-85228e6b-6a49-4d75-af59-53be54ca3953.gif)
.

### Steps to reproduce

- Place a CharacterBody3D on a flat surface
- Place a cylindrical StaticBody3D collider near the CharacterBody3D, and rotate it 90° along the X axis so the bottom or top of the cylinder becomes a wall.
- In play mode move the character so that it collides with the flat end of the cylinder, and try to slide along it diagonally like a wall.

(For some reason if the cylinder has its scale set to (2.8, 2, 2.8) and is placed about 1 unit above the surface of the floor the issue is more present)

### Minimal reproduction project

[CharacterAndCylinderIssue.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/7968362/CharacterAndCylinderIssue.zip)
comments: I noticed that this problem doesn't occur if the collider is a polygonal cylinder, like with a CSG cylinder.

The problem is related to the contact points returned by the engine, it seems to occur only with this rotation,  this could be caused by a bad separation axis.

In the following image you can see the contact points as pink dots::

![test1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/177040708-7447e116-ac32-4c2a-9113-d4252e8decdb.png)

Same scene but using a CSG Cylinder:

![test2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/177040719-0c229a07-9c78-4e3d-9971-2c9942ca6a05.png)

As in the first one, there is no contact point in the cylinder, the body cannot slide and ends up being stuck.

I believe I am encountering something similar but with more than just cylinders, I've been getting it with all collision shapes. Sliding against them just seems very failure-prone and leads to objects getting stuck all the time.
@novaplusplus could you share a minimal reproduction project, just the bare minimum with the default script movement?

I am having similar problem..
![stuckwall](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10412778/198068255-3ef814dd-04c2-4d8e-ab13-9e57ffd12633.gif)
@fabriceci Here is a minimal reproduction with default script movement:
[moveSlideStuck.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9870935/moveSlideStuck.zip)

> I believe I am encountering something similar but with more than just cylinders, I've been getting it with all collision shapes. Sliding against them just seems very failure-prone and leads to objects getting stuck all the time.

Same thing is happening to me. Brush up against a wall? Stuck.
@akien-mga was this closed intentionally? I'm still seeing CharacterBody3D getting stuck agaisn't edges on 4.0.2, including on the above example by prominentdetail
I can confirm the issue still occurs with @prominentdetail's MRP in 4.0.2. I would recommend testing https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/68958 locally and see if it resolves the issue.
Unfortunately still able to reproduce on https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/68958 (v4.0.beta.custom_build [b8121013f]) You're able to get stuck on the corner here pretty easily

having this issue on 4.1. both cylinder and capsule playershapes get stuck on walls and corners of staticbody3ds.
edit: it has no problem sliding against csgboxes normally, but corners still get stuck and jittery

Confirmed still issue in 4.1.1

As far as I can tell so far, this issue doesn't appear to be reproducible when using godot-jolt physics 🤞 . cc https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7308
I tested @prominentdetail's MRP in v4.1.1.stable.official [bd6af8e0e] with godot-jolt physics and it's working flawlessly.

I have this problem with the characterbody3d node as well. But my set up does not involve walls. It simply gets stuck moving on a flat surface. I'm using the Kenney Starter Kit for 3D Platformers (https://github.com/KenneyNL/Starter-Kit-3D-Platformer), which includes a platform prefab that I'm using with my own characters made from scratch. I can dislodge my character by jumping. However, I'm not sure how to resolve the problem. 

I actually think timing might have something to do with it. It seems to happen after 17 seconds of game play. I will move my character back and forth over the platform, and every 17 seconds, it will get caught on the floor, and I have to jump to dislodge it. 

I have attached a video of this happening:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/7929931/d31e771c-35be-4de4-8cc6-2bd952e3a34c

Is it possible that it is my computer?
I'm still getting bodies with cylinder as collision shapes stuck while sliding against the wall on v4.3.beta3.official [82cedc83c].

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/849a8e20-01ec-44eb-baf5-f6b657a23b3c)

I am also experiencing this, when trying to move when there is a edge just clipping  the top of the capsule collider my player controller uses. The CharacterBody3D does not slide, it gets stuck.

@wapcaf This should be resolved in 4.4.beta if you switch the 3D physics engine to **Jolt Physics** in the Project Settings. If not, please open a new issue with a minimal reproduction project attached.

review_comments: If the p_collector->callback is null you can bail here and save some computrons calculating the normalized axis as it won't be used if there is no callback. I just did the same change for my analytic sphere collision.
